key_insight: Graphene on Ge(001)/Si(001) shows a spatially non-uniform charge-transfer landscape, where pristine regions are n-doped by electron transfer from Ge, but oxidation can flip the interface to p-type behavior.
engineering_relevance: Understanding and controlling this local electronic coupling helps optimize graphene growth and delamination on Si-compatible substrates for electronic devices and protective transfer layers.
method: UPS + KPFM mapped work-function variation across the surface
ARPES + DFT established the pristine-interface doping trend
STS with machine-learning classification separated distinct local electronic regimes
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent agreement across UPS, KPFM, ARPES, STS, and DFT, with local signals tied to nanofaceted morphology and different interface chemistries.
watch_item: The doping polarity depends strongly on oxidation and local morphology, so device performance may vary unless the interface state is tightly controlled during synthesis and transfer.
paper_title: Electronic Coupling and Charge-Transfer Landscape of Graphene on Ge(001)/Si(001): Multiscale Analysis Assisted by Machine Learning
